$comment: Guard-coverage ratchet (#564). `unreviewed` is a backlog to burn down, not a mute button: a new unguarded site fails, and an entry that becomes guarded or disappears fails as stale. `internallyDerived` records sites whose constrained ids cannot dangle (session- or internally-sourced), each with the reason — a prior read is NOT a reason, it leaves a TOCTOU window. Regenerate with: npm run prisma:guard-coverage -- --write

internallyDerived.POST /announcements/blog::blog.create: Blog's only foreign key is userId, set from req.user.id. A session-derived id cannot dangle, and the model carries no unique constraint.
internallyDerived.POST /announcements/global-notice::globa: GlobalNotice's only foreign key is createdById, set from req.user.id. A session-derived id cannot dangle, and the model carries no unique constraint.
internallyDerived.POST /forums/{id}/catchup::forumLastRead: No client-supplied id reaches a constrained column: userId is session-derived, and forumTopicId/forumPostId come from a forumTopic read issued in the same request. #564 is about a well-formed request naming something absent; here the caller names nothing. A topic deleted concurrently mid-transaction is a different concern and would not be a client error.
internallyDerived.POST /auth::userSession.create: The only foreign key is userId, taken from the account just authenticated in this request, so it cannot dangle.
internallyDerived.POST /messages/drafts::pmDraft.create: The only foreign key is userId, from the session. `toUserId` is a plain Int with no relation, so it cannot raise P2003.
internallyDerived.POST /messages/mass::massMessage.create: The only foreign key is senderId, from the session.
internallyDerived.POST /posts::post.create: The only foreign key is userId, from the session; Post carries no unique constraint.
internallyDerived.POST /site-history::siteHistory.create: The only foreign key is authorId, from the session; SiteHistory carries no unique constraint.
internallyDerived.DELETE /profile::user.update: Addressed by req.user.id — the row belongs to the caller's own live session, so it is present by construction.
internallyDerived.POST /install::userSettings.create: Created inside the install transaction with no foreign key set and no unique constraint on the model.
internallyDerived.POST /install::user.create: Its three foreign keys (userRankId, userSettingsId, profileId) are all rows created earlier in the same transaction. The unique username/email are client-supplied, but the route refuses with 409 unless settings.installedAt is null, so there is no existing user for them to collide with.
